answers.core: This is a core part of Godot.
answers.workaround:
I had worked around this but I had to 
1. Create a scene that just contains an AnimationTree
2. Pre-create a BlendTree as root
3. Add a BlendSpace1D into it
4. Connect that BlendSpace1D to the output of the BlendTree in the GUI
5. Go into my script that needed an animation tree a preload that scene
6. Create an instance of that scene when I configured my animationTree
7. Configure the AnimationTree

My problems with this is
1. The scene I created is not really that flexible. If I need a BlendSpace2D variant I will have to create a brand new scene
2. I have to do the preload -> instance dance to get it into memory, this adds more variables on my class, not sure if it makes things less performant or anything but it makes things a bit more complicated.
